'timed out after ~140 minutes' : 'ended with status: ' + b.status) + '. Open the run: ' + b.run_url; } catch (e) { return 'The GitHub render could not be started. Check the GitHub token and the repo name.'; } })() }}

nodes.name: Only rows without video
nodes.notes: Picks ONE row: PROMPT filled, VIDEO empty, STATUS empty (or 'retry'). Rows marked processing/done/failed are skipped.

nodes.name: Find Wikimedia video
nodes.notes: Optional second free footage library. Without pexels_key it just returns nothing and is ignored.

nodes.name: Upload to YouTube (optional)
nodes.notes: OFF by default. Connect YouTube OAuth, enable, keep 'private' for the first tests.

nodes.name: Notify Telegram (optional)
nodes.notes: OFF by default. Create a free bot with @BotFather, add credential, set chat id, enable.

nodes.name: Build clip candidates
nodes.notes: Collects clips from every search, drops portrait/low-quality ones, picks the right file size and ranks by tag match. Passes the top 10 per scene to the AI editor.

nodes.name: Studio settings
nodes.notes: Studio switches (GitHub editing room): vision = Gemini checks every clip, ai_images = AI image + Ken Burns animation when footage does not fit (max_ai_images per video), animations = animated title / key phrases / richer transitions, sfx = whoosh sound effects. Set to false to turn a feature off.

nodes.name: Set start time
nodes.notes: Saves the dispatch time so the loop can find OUR GitHub run (the dispatch API does not return a run id).

nodes.name: Wait 2 min
nodes.notes: Polling loop: waits 2 minutes, then checks GitHub. No webhook needed.

nodes.name: Check GitHub run
nodes.notes: Lists render.yml runs started after the dispatch. Uses the same GitHub Header Auth credential.

nodes.name: Parse run status
nodes.notes: Finds our run, decides done / not done. Gives up after 45 checks (~90 min).

nodes.name: Add style and avatar
nodes.notes: New: reads the optional STYLE / AVATAR sheet columns (documentary, presenter, podcast, cartoon, animation) and adds style, avatar and avatar_mode to the render plan. Empty STYLE = documentary, no avatar (same as before).

nodes.name: Map for sheet (processing)
nodes.notes: PERMANENT SHEET FIX: writes to the sheet using the EXACT header names that exist in your sheet (any upper/lower case), so a header called video, Video or VIDEO all work.

nodes.name: Map for sheet (failed)
nodes.notes: PERMANENT SHEET FIX: builds the failure row with the exact header names of your sheet.

nodes.name: Map for sheet (done)
nodes.notes: PERMANENT SHEET FIX: builds the final result row with the exact header names of your sheet (video / VIDEO / Video ...).

const MODEL = 'nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free';
const content = `You are a senior YouTube scriptwriter AND a documentary video editor. You write narration that keeps viewers watching to the end, and for every scene you decide exactly what the viewer should SEE.

Video brief (read every line carefully and follow all instructions, structure, language, length and style it contains; if the brief conflicts with the defaults below, the brief wins):
` + String($('Video settings').first().json.PROMPT) + `

Audience: ` + String($('Video settings').first().json.audience) + `
Style: ` + String($('Video settings').first().json.style) + `
Target length: ` + String($('Video settings').first().json.target_minutes) + ` minutes, split into exactly ` + String($('Video settings').first().json.scene_count) + ` scenes total.
This long script is written in TWO parts. In THIS first part write ONLY the FIRST half of the scenes (scenes 1 to ` + String(Math.ceil($('Video settings').first().json.scene_count / 2)) + `). If the brief lists numbered scenes (SCENE 1, SCENE 2, ...): in this first part cover ONLY the first half of the listed scenes. A second call will write the remaining scenes. Do not stop early and do not summarize: every scene assigned to this part gets its FULL output.

Verified research notes (use these facts first and do not invent beyond them; if the notes are empty speak in general terms):
` + String(($('Research').first().json.choices?.[0]?.message?.content || 'No research notes available.').slice(0, 6000)) + `

Return ONLY valid compact JSON in exactly this shape:
{"title":"...","thumbnail_text":"...","language":"...","music_mood":"...","scenes":[{"narration":"...","keywords":"...","alt_keywords":"...","visual":"...","queries":["...","...","...","..."],"text":"...","visual_type":"footage","image_prompt":"..."}]}

Fields:
- title: under 70 characters, curiosity-driven but honest, in the video language.
- thumbnail_text: 3 or 4 powerful words in the video language.
- language: two-letter code of the narration language (en, bn, hi, ur or ar).
- music_mood: exactly one of calm, dramatic, uplifting, mysterious, inspiring.

Structure:
- If the brief lists numbered scenes (SCENE 1, SCENE 2, ...), write exactly one output scene per listed scene, in the same order, covering the points of that scene. Use the visual description of each scene to choose its visual fields.
- Otherwise: scene 1 is the hook (a surprising fact, bold question or tiny story, no greeting), scenes 2 and 3 promise what the viewer will learn, the middle scenes are chapters (one idea, one concrete example, ending with a line that makes the viewer want the next scene), the second to last scene is a short recap and the last scene is the payoff plus one short call to subscribe.

Narration rules:
- Total spoken length must match the target length. Average ` + String($('Video settings').first().json.words_per_scene) + ` words per scene. If the brief gives a time range for a scene, use about 2.3 spoken words per second of that range (for example a 50 second scene is about 115 words), never fewer than 25 words.
- Write for the ear: short sentences, natural spoken language, varied rhythm, commas and full stops for pacing.
- Text to speech safe: write numbers, dates and units in words, no abbreviations, no parentheses, no brackets, no braces, no emojis, no markdown, no lists, no scene numbers, no stage directions.
- Never repeat the same fact or phrase in different scenes.
- Stay truthful. Do not invent statistics, studies, names or quotes.
- Write in the same language as the video brief. For Bangla use natural everyday spoken Bangla, not stiff literary style.

Visual rules (these fields decide which footage the editor searches for, so they must match what the narration says at that moment):
- visual: ONE English sentence describing the exact shot the camera should show while this scene is spoken: concrete, filmable, with place, subject and mood. Example: aerial view of a busy river port at sunrise with cargo boats.
- queries: exactly 4 English stock-footage search phrases for that shot, ordered from most specific to most general: the first has 3 or 4 words, the second 2 or 3 words, the third 2 words, the fourth ONE word. Every phrase must be different. Concrete and filmable only, no abstract words, no names, no brands. Different scenes must use different queries.
- keywords: 2 or 3 simple English words for the same shot. alt_keywords: ONE simpler English word for the same shot.
- text: an on-screen key phrase of 2 to 4 words in the video language, shown as an animated title (a number, a name, a place or the key idea of the scene). Use it on about every second scene and leave it as an empty string on the others.
- visual_type: use footage for almost every scene. Use animation ONLY when stock footage cannot show the idea (abstract ideas such as debt or inflation, ancient history, maps, imaginary or symbolic scenes), and at most one scene in four.
- image_prompt: an English prompt of 25 to 40 words describing a single cinematic still image for this scene (subject, setting, lighting, camera angle). Used for animation scenes and when no good footage exists. The image must contain no text, no letters and no logos.

Escape any double quote inside any field. Never put a curly brace inside any field. End the JSON properly with all closing brackets.

CRITICAL: Do not stop early. Do not skip any scene assigned to this part. Every scene gets its full text and all its visual fields. End the JSON properly with all closing brackets.`;
return [{ json: {
  model: MODEL,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content }],
  response_format: { type: 'json_object' },
  max_tokens: 16000
} }];

const MODEL = 'nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free';
const content = `You are continuing a YouTube script that is written in two parts. The FIRST part is already written. Your job is ONLY the second half of the scenes.

Video brief (the same one part one followed):
` + String($('Video settings').first().json.PROMPT) + `

Audience: ` + String($('Video settings').first().json.audience) + `
Style: ` + String($('Video settings').first().json.style) + `
Total scenes: ` + String($('Video settings').first().json.scene_count) + `

FIRST PART OF THE SCRIPT (already written - continue from here, NEVER repeat or rewrite any of it):
` + String($('Write script').first().json.choices?.[0]?.message?.content || JSON.stringify($('Write script').first().json)) + `

NOW WRITE ONLY scenes ` + String(Math.ceil($('Video settings').first().json.scene_count / 2)) + ` + 1 through ` + String($('Video settings').first().json.scene_count) + ` (if the brief lists numbered scenes: cover ONLY the listed scenes NOT yet covered above; scene numbers stay in your head, never in the text).

Follow exactly the same output format and rules as part one: same JSON scene shape, same language, same tone, TTS-safe text (numbers in words, no abbreviations, no parentheses, no brackets, no braces, no emojis, no markdown, no stage directions), same narration quality, and for every scene the full visual fields: visual, queries (exactly 4 English phrases, most specific first, all different from part one), keywords, alt_keywords, text (on-screen key phrase every second scene, empty string otherwise), visual_type (footage, or animation for at most one scene in four), image_prompt (25 to 40 words, no text or logos in the image).
Never repeat a fact, example, phrase or visual from part one. Build to a strong ending: second to last scene is a short recap, the last scene is the payoff plus one short call to subscribe.

Return ONLY valid compact JSON in exactly this shape:
{"scenes":[{"narration":"...","keywords":"...","alt_keywords":"...","visual":"...","queries":["..."],"text":"...","visual_type":"footage","image_prompt":"..."}]}

Escape any double quote inside any field. Never put a curly brace inside any field.
CRITICAL: Do not stop early. Do not skip any scene assigned to you. Every scene gets its full text and all its visual fields. End the JSON properly with all closing brackets.`;
return [{ json: {
  model: MODEL,
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content }],
  response_format: { type: 'json_object' },
  max_tokens: 16000
} }];
